newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan police teargas Sunni Moslem demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan police teargas Sunni Moslem demonstrators.

text.p: Pakistani police used batons and teargas to disperse about 150 Sunni Moslem demonstrators in the city of Rawalpindi, near the capital Islamabad, on Friday, witnesses said.
They said the demonstrators were chanting slogans against Pakistan's Shi'ite Moslem minority, which is preparing to observe the Shi'ite mourning festival of Ashura on Sunday.
There were no immediate reports of arrests or casualties.
Army troops have been deployed in Lahore and several other towns and cities in Punjab province this week to try to prevent clashes between militant Sunni and Shi'ite groups.
Police said they had detained 12 members of the Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group in Lahore for attempting to stage an outlawed procession after Friday prayers.
The Punjab provincial government has ordered traffic to be diverted and shops closed during Shi'ite processions planned in various cities over the next few days to prevent any unrest.
Sectarian violence has killed more than 70 people this year in tit-for-tat shootings and grenade attacks by rival groups.
Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of Pakistan's estimated 138 million people, most of whom are Sunnis.
